doc: Bilinear resize of an NCHW tensor to (out_h, out_w) with align_corners=False (half-pixel centers, no antialiasing).
name: bilinear_resize

doc: Bilinear 2D resize of a (C, H, W) map to out=[OH, OW], align_corners=False, no antialiasing. For each output pixel: sy=(oh+0.5)*H/OH-0.5, sx=(ow+0.5)*W/OW-0.5; iy=floor(sy), ix=floor(sx), weights wy=sy-iy, wx=sx-ix; indices clamped to borders; output is the bilinear blend of the 4 neighbors.
name: bilinear_resize2d
reference:
def fn(x, out):
    import torch
    C, H, W = x.shape
    OH, OW = out
    sy = (torch.arange(OH, dtype=x.dtype) + 0.5) * H / OH - 0.5
    sx = (torch.arange(OW, dtype=x.dtype) + 0.5) * W / OW - 0.5
    iy = sy.floor().long().clamp(0, H - 1)
    ix = sx.floor().long().clamp(0, W - 1)
    wy = (sy - sy.floor()).clamp(0, 1)
    wx = (sx - sx.floor()).clamp(0, 1)
    i0 = iy.clamp(0, H - 2); i1 = (iy + 1).clamp(0, H - 1)
    j0 = ix.clamp(0, W - 2); j1 = (ix + 1).clamp(0, W - 1)
    a = x[:, i0, :][:, :, j0]; b = x[:, i0, :][:, :, j1]
    c = x[:, i1, :][:, :, j0]; d = x[:, i1, :][:, :, j1]
    wy = wy.view(1, OH, 1); wx = wx.view(1, 1, OW)
    return (1 - wy) * ((1 - wx) * a + wx * b) + wy * ((1 - wx) * c + wx * d)

doc: Bilinear resize of a (C, H, W) map to out=[56, 56], align_corners=False, no antialiasing. For each output pixel: sy=(oh+0.5)*H/56-0.5, sx=(ow+0.5)*W/56-0.5; iy=floor(sy), ix=floor(sx), weights wy=sy-iy, wx=sx-ix; indices clamped to borders; output is the bilinear blend of the 4 neighbors.

def fn(x, out=(56, 56)):
    import torch
    C, H, W = x.shape
    OH, OW = out
    sy = (torch.arange(OH, dtype=torch.float32) + 0.5) * H / OH - 0.5

    i0 = iy.clamp(0, H - 1); i1 = (iy + 1).clamp(0, H - 1)
    j0 = ix.clamp(0, W - 1); j1 = (ix + 1).clamp(0, W - 1)
    a = x[:, i0, :][:, :, j0]; b = x[:, i0, :][:, :, j1]
    c = x[:, i1, :][:, :, j0]; d = x[:, i1, :][:, :, j1]
    wy = wy.view(1, OH, 1); wx = wx.view(1, 1, OW)
    return (1 - wy) * ((1 - wx) * a + wx * b) + wy * ((1 - wx) * c + wx * d)

doc: Bilinear 2x upsample of a (C, H, W) map to (C, 2H, 2W), align_corners=False, no antialiasing. For each output pixel: sy=(oh+0.5)/2-0.5, sx=(ow+0.5)/2-0.5; iy=floor(sy), ix=floor(sx), weights wy=sy-iy, wx=sx-ix; indices clamped to borders; output is the bilinear blend of the 4 neighbors.
name: bilinear_up2x
reference:
def fn(x):
    import torch
    C, H, W = x.shape
    OH, OW = 2 * H, 2 * W
    sy = (torch.arange(OH, dtype=torch.float32) + 0.5) / 2 - 0.5
    sx = (torch.arange(OW, dtype=torch.float32) + 0.5) / 2 - 0.5
    iy = sy.floor().long(); ix = sx.floor().long()
    wy = (sy - sy.floor()).clamp(0, 1); wx = (sx - sx.floor()).clamp(0, 1)
    i0 = iy.clamp(0, H - 1); i1 = (iy + 1).clamp(0, H - 1)
    j0 = ix.clamp(0, W - 1); j1 = (ix + 1).clamp(0, W - 1)
    a = x[:, i0, :][:, :, j0]; b = x[:, i0, :][:, :, j1]
    c = x[:, i1, :][:, :, j0]; d = x[:, i1, :][:, :, j1]
    wy = wy.view(1, OH, 1); wx = wx.view(1, 1, OW)
    return (1 - wy) * ((1 - wx) * a + wx * b) + wy * ((1 - wx) * c + wx * d)

def fn(ids, table, num_classes):
    ids = ids.long().reshape(-1)
    oh = torch.zeros(ids.shape[0], num_classes, dtype=table.dtype, device=table.device)
    oh[torch.arange(ids.shape[0]), ids] = 1.0
    return oh @ table
